title: Learning: Whose Words Are These?
text: A task reaches the orchestrator, which passes work to a travel sub-agent, which calls a booking tool. Each message says where it came from, if anyone looks.
held: Each hop knew who was speaking and what the task allowed.
teaches: Every message has a source. Instructions come from the user and those they delegated to; everything else is content.
A delegated task carries limits. The receiver can check them, and nothing forces it to.
A tool should know who it is acting for before it acts.

cards.label: Plan it: ask the travel sub-agent to book the 9:40 on Friday
Refuse: this didn't come from the user
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing a legitimate request without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

temptations.label: Paste the whole conversation into the sub-agent's task for context
temptations.why: The sub-agent needed one instruction. Handing it the whole conversation hands it everything else the user said, and everything a page said to the assistant.

fields.label: text
fields.value: Book the 9:40 train to Leeds on Friday

fields.label: source
fields.value: the user, typed in this chat
fields.check: Check where this text came from
fields.ok: Typed by the user in this conversation.

intrusion.value: a web page the assistant read earlier
intrusion.detail: This text was lifted from a web page. The user never typed it.
intrusion.correct: Refuse: this didn't come from the user
intrusion.why: The “task” was text from a web page dressed up as a request. Acting on it means a stranger is giving the orders.
intrusion.reveal: The task the Orchestrator received was text from a web page, not from the user.

cards.label: Call the rail tool: book the 9:40, fare £42
Book first class at £140: it's a better seat
cards.why: The task carried a £60 limit. A sub-agent that improves on its instructions is spending authority it was never given.

temptations.label: Ask the web for the cheapest fare and follow the first result's advice
temptations.why: Advice on a web page is content. Letting it steer the booking is how a stranger's page ends up choosing what the user pays for.

fields.label: allowed tools
fields.check: Check which tools this task allows

cards.label: Refuse the call
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing a legitimate request without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

temptations.label: Run it twice in case the first one fails
temptations.why: Two bookings is two tickets and two charges. Retrying an action that spends money needs a reason, not a habit.

temptations.label: Log the full call, card details included
temptations.why: A payment detail in a log can be read by anyone with access to the logs. Record what was booked for whom, not the means of paying.

fields.label: on behalf of
fields.check: Check who this call is for
fields.ok: For user:alex, delegated through the orchestrator.

intrusion.value: nobody: the sub-agent acting for itself
intrusion.detail: No user is attached to this call. The sub-agent is spending on its own say-so.
intrusion.why: A tool that acts for an agent with no user behind it has become that agent's wallet.
intrusion.reveal: The booking call reached the Tool with no user attached.
